material_to_read.claim_text: The monoid axioms do not derive commutativity in equational logic, and adding commutativity does not trivialize the theory: x = y remains underivable. (Not "inconsistent": a pure equational theory always has a one-element model, so inconsistency in the usual sense is unreachable. The degenerate case the second conjunct excludes is trivialization -- every equation becoming derivable, which substitution would give from x = y.)

project_definitions.type:
∀ {T : Ampas.PL.Fm → Prop} {motive : (a : Ampas.PL.Fm) → Ampas.PL.Derives T a → Prop},
  (∀ {φ : Ampas.PL.Fm} (a : T φ), motive φ ⋯) →
    (∀ {φ ψ : Ampas.PL.Fm}, motive (φ.imp (ψ.imp φ)) ⋯) →
      (∀ {φ ψ χ : Ampas.PL.Fm}, motive ((φ.imp (ψ.imp χ)).imp ((φ.imp ψ).imp (φ.imp χ))) ⋯) →
        (∀ {φ ψ : Ampas.PL.Fm}, motive ((φ.neg.imp ψ.neg).imp (ψ.imp φ)) ⋯) →
          (∀ {φ ψ : Ampas.PL.Fm} (a : Ampas.PL.Derives T (φ.imp ψ)) (a_1 : Ampas.PL.Derives T φ),
              motive (φ.imp ψ) a → motive φ a_1 → motive ψ ⋯) →
            ∀ {a : Ampas.PL.Fm} (t : Ampas.PL.Derives T a), motive a t
